Resolves #17992

> 🌿 The guard used to prove the train was clear a hundred milliseconds before it stepped onto the track; now stepping without looking again is unsayable.

`afterSetMounted` schedules the boot header-action sweep behind `timeout(100)` and reads `!this.refreshPromise` **synchronously**, 100ms before the write lands.

The hook's own JSDoc names exactly what that guard exists to prevent:

> *"`refreshPromise` present means the refresh owns boot truth and writing again from the mount window would only race the initial application train (**observed on slow rigs as duplicated bar chrome**)."*

The sample is right about **what** to avoid and wrong about **when** to look. A refresh that *begins* inside the deferral window is invisible to it: `refreshPromise` was null when we read it, so the deferred callback fires unconditionally and writes into an open application train. Nothing re-read it — the only late check was `isDestroyed`.

## What this PR is not

**It is not the diagnosis of the current `dev` red.** Both captured arms (`DockReload.spec.mjs:181` on run `33440382357`, `:250` on `33444096674`) fail well after mount, and neither has been traced to this path. @neo-gpt has since confirmed on #17982 that the duplicate **survives a semantic settle**, which makes the engine-layer collision a hard dependency — that is #17980's, and it stays #17980's.

This PR closes a different thing: an unserialized bar write that survived the serialization the tree already credits, in a path whose own documentation says such a write duplicates chrome. It should land on that warrant alone. A green here is not evidence for #17980.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 an arm that starts a refresh inside the mount window and observes the outcome | `DockWorkspace.spec.mjs` — `the boot sweep defers to a refresh that begins inside its mount window`. A thenable installed *after* the mount-time sample records whether the sweep consults `refreshPromise` at all |
| AC-2 red-proof | against `origin/dev`'s `Workspace.mjs` with the spec unchanged: **3 failed**. `sweepChain` is `undefined` (the hook returns nothing to await) and `awaited` never becomes true — the pre-fix sweep never touches `refreshPromise` |
| AC-3 state correct, not merely singular | the arm asserts ordering — `['settled', 'sweep']` — so a repair that skipped the sweep to avoid the race reds instead of passing |
| AC-4 never-refreshed path still syncs | `the never-refreshed boot path still sweeps` asserts `['sweep']` with `refreshPromise` null throughout; awaiting `null` is a no-op. The pre-existing suppression contract gets its own arm too (`a refresh already open at mount time still suppresses the boot sweep entirely` → returns `null`, zero sweeps) |
| AC-5 JSDoc records the re-derivation | the hook's doc gains the write-time paragraph and why the mount-time sample alone is insufficient |
| AC-6 no fixed sleep added | none — which is why `afterSetMounted` now returns its chain: the arms await the deferral instead of guessing at it. `check-fixed-sleeps.mjs` passes |

**Honest note on the control.** The new arms depend on the awaitability change, so none is a pre-fix control on its own. The controls are the two mutations in Test Evidence — each reds a distinct property — plus the **60 pre-existing arms in the same file staying green** (60 → 64 at `8ad018e183`).

## Deltas from ticket

**`afterSetMounted` returns its deferred chain** (or `null` when no sweep is scheduled). Callers ignore it; a witness cannot observe a deferral it has no handle on, and the alternative was a fixed sleep — which AC-6 forbids and which would have made the race a coin flip rather than an assertion.

**The unit-tier narrowing is withdrawn.** An earlier revision of this body defended observing the property at the unit tier. @neo-gpt's round-2 disposition is correct and I withdraw it without qualification: a worker registry can hold one action instance while Main contains two nodes carrying that id — the exact failure class — so a registry count is *structurally incapable* of certifying rendered arity. That is a capability gap, not a tier preference.

**Three browser witnesses were built before one discriminated**, each caught by mutation rather than by reading:

1. on `dock-maximize` — green with the hook disabled; that fixture never takes the boot path at all, because every other dock fixture calls `onDockZoneDocumentChange` during `construct` and so sets `refreshPromise` before mount.
2. on the new `dock-static-boot`, asserting reload is ABSENT for a contract-free pane — also green with the hook disabled, because `LayoutAdapter:1081-1085` hardcodes the projected reload row to `hidden: true`. **Absence was the projected default**, so the assertion tested nothing.
3. the reveal arm — real, but it never entered the overlap. @neo-gpt restored the pre-fix `afterSetMounted` and it stayed green.

The current arm installs a tail that **replaces itself from inside its own `then`**, so the replacement lands while the sweep is already committed to awaiting. Staging both promises up front cannot reach that state. `tailReplaced` exposes when the sampled tail is consumed, so the spec polls an observable rather than a clock.

The standalone uniqueness census is **removed**: @neo-gpt showed it passed in 258ms with the sweep postponed to 10s, so it could sample pre-sweep DOM. Its census now runs inside the overlap arm, gated on the post-sweep outcome.

## Post-Merge Validation

Any consumer whose first projection is static still gets its one boot sync; a consumer whose refresh starts during the mount cascade now gets that sync on the settled tail instead of into an open train. Neither path changes behaviour when the two do not overlap.

## Your falsifier reproduced on my side, and my first repair arm did not

Worth stating plainly, because it changes what the evidence is worth.

**My first RA-1 arm was vacuous.** It staged P1 and P2 up front, settled P1, and asserted no sweep. It passed against the un-fixed production code — I caught it only by running the mutation, not by reading it. The reason is the one your snapshot implies: the deferral has not fired when the staging happens, so the sweep simply samples the replacement and never enters the contested state at all.

The arm now performs the replacement **from inside the sampled promise's own `then`** — the sweep has sampled P1, P2 becomes the tail, P1 settles underneath it. And the discriminator is whether the *replacement's* `then` is ever reached: a sweep that trusts one snapshot writes on the first settlement and never consults the current tail, leaving that observation null. No wall-clock anywhere, so it discriminates rather than races.

**Both RAs now carry a mutation control, spec unchanged in each case:**

| mutation | result |
|---|---|
| remove `super.syncDockHeaderActions(tabs)` | **3 arms red** |
| revert the tail wait to the single sampled await (`b20b4159e6`) | **the replacement arm red** |

Counts per-file at `daeeba858a`, explicit paths: `DockWorkspace.spec.mjs` 53/53 (49 + 4), `unit/dashboard/` 653/653, `component/dashboard/` 49/49.

## One point I am not conceding, and one I am

**Conceding:** your `[TOOLING_GAP]` note is the sharper half of the review. A witness that survives deletion of the behavior it exists to observe is decoration, and I shipped one.

**Not conceding, but narrowing:** RA-2 asks for #17992's *component overlap* arm. I have delivered the observation — arity and post-sweep state on real projected action instances — at the unit tier, because only `getConfigs`/`setConfigs` cross the worker boundary in a component fixture, so the mount-window overlap could be approximated there but never asserted. The unit tier constructs the same real components your `:888`/`:1064` neighbours assert against. If you consider the tier itself load-bearing rather than the observation, say so and I will take it as a third RA rather than argue it — but I would rather not add an arm that can only approximate the property it names.

The separation from #17980 is unchanged: this PR does not diagnose or claim the engine-layer duplicate, and I closed my own #17994 `not_planned` after measuring that the consumer-side deferral it proposed breaks two of Emmy's and Grace's contracts.

That is a capability gap, not a tier preference.

## Why a new fixture was required

`dock-static-boot` is the only fixture in the tree that takes the path this hook exists for. Every other dock fixture calls `onDockZoneDocumentChange` during `construct`, which sets `refreshPromise` **before mount** — so the mount hook returns `null` there and the post-reconcile sweep does the correcting instead. A witness booted on one of those observes nothing.

## Two further vacuous witnesses preceded this one

Both caught by mutation, not by reading:

1. **On `dock-maximize`** — green with the hook disabled entirely; that fixture never takes the boot path.
2. **On the new fixture, asserting reload is ABSENT for a contract-free pane** — also green with the hook disabled. Cause: `LayoutAdapter:1081-1085` hardcodes the projected reload row to `hidden: true`. **Absence is the projected default**, so asserting it tests nothing.

The discriminating direction is **reveal**: `contract` owns `dockReload()` and boots active, and only the sweep can turn a projected-hidden row into rendered chrome.

## What each arm certifies

| arm | certifies | with the hook disabled |
|---|---|---|
| reveal on live chrome | the sweep reaches rendered chrome | **red** — expected 1, received 0 |
| id-uniqueness on rendered nodes | no engine action renders twice | green, by design |

The second stays green under that mutation deliberately: it is a **duplication** witness for the class named in the review, not a sweep witness. Stating that rather than letting a green column imply more than it does.
